funding.fund: Efficient, Structured and Controllable AI Systems (comp. 2582)
funding.match_funding: Up to 70% of costs (by business size)
funding.why_it_fits: Only fits if the routing/scheduling engine involves a genuinely novel AI/ML mechanism (e.g. resource-adaptive or causal models) rather than integration of existing optimisers.
funding.eligibility_notes: UK-registered SMEs incl. NI; single applicant, no subcontractors; 1–3 month project, TRL 1–3; literature reviews/routine integration/prompt engineering out of scope. Closes 11:00.
funding.next_step: Decide this week whether the AI work is novel enough; if yes, draft via IFS and use Invest NI Bid Review Service.

funding.why_it_fits: Funds founder time to build the care-routing product faster, with mentoring and investor access for a later equity round.
funding.eligibility_notes: NI start-ups that can show, by year 3, revenue or funding >£1m, ≥60% of sales outside NI (target GB/ROI private domiciliary providers) and external investment. Six months full-time.
funding.next_step: Apply via Ormeau Labs Founder Labs page before 20 Nov; frame GB/ROI care-provider market to meet 60% external-sales test.

funding.fund: BridgeAI Deployment Catalyst: AI for Operational Systems
funding.match_funding: Not stated on summary page – check IFS brief (comp. 2599)
funding.why_it_fits: Strongest UK fit: deploying AI that plans/coordinates operations – i.e. scheduling domiciliary care runs to cut mileage, fuel and missed visits.
funding.eligibility_notes: Collaborative only: lead must be a UK-registered AI SME with existing AI/ML at TRL 5–6, plus one UK medium/large deployer (e.g. a large care provider); 2–3 partners. Opened 21 Oct 2026; closes 11:00. UK-wide – NI eligibility not separately stated; confirm in brief.
funding.next_step: Line up a medium/large domiciliary care provider as deployer now; read full IFS brief; book Invest NI Bid Review.

funding.fund: BridgeAI Deployment Catalyst: AI for Decision Critical Systems
funding.match_funding: Not stated on listing – check IFS brief
funding.why_it_fits: Possible fit if framed around high-stakes care decisions (visit prioritisation, discharge-to-home capacity).
funding.eligibility_notes: Same consortium rules as Operational Systems strand (UK AI SME lead + medium/large deployer, 2–3 orgs). Pick one strand – Operational is the closer fit.
funding.next_step: Compare scope with the Operational Systems strand; apply to the better-fitting one.

funding.match_funding: Business contributes to costs – rate not stated on listing; check KTP guidance
funding.why_it_fits: Places a graduate with QUB/Ulster academic support to build routing-optimisation and mileage/cost analytics.
funding.eligibility_notes: Led by a UK university/RTO/Catapult with the business as partner; UK-wide incl. NI. Opened 19 Oct 2026.
funding.next_step: Contact QUB or Ulster University KTP office this month to scope a project before the 27 Jan deadline.

funding.match_funding: Up to 100% of costs depending on call
funding.why_it_fits: Long shot: care-delivery and digital/AI topics; no integrated-care topic listed.
funding.eligibility_notes: UK entities eligible (Associated Country) but only in consortia of ≥3 entities in different countries incl. ≥1 EU member state. 13 Apr 2027 is first-stage/single-stage close; some later calls 22 Sep 2027.
funding.next_step: Low priority; only pursue if an EU consortium invites you.

funding.amount: Project Definition up to £100k; Grant for R&D covers labour, materials, IP, trials, consultancy + 15% overhead
funding.why_it_fits: Core NI route to fund software R&D: feasibility, prototyping and project planning for the scheduling platform.
funding.eligibility_notes: Invest NI clients (or businesses that qualify): tradeable services, ≥25% sales outside NI (or £250k) and ≥10 staff within 5 years.
funding.next_step: Call Business Support Team to check client eligibility and request a client executive.

funding.why_it_fits: Can pay a technical service provider for specialist work (e.g. routing algorithms, mapping integration).
funding.eligibility_notes: Local SMEs; contributes toward technical service providers.

funding.why_it_fits: Improves odds on BridgeAI / Innovate UK bids.

funding.next_step: Email draft BridgeAI application at least 2–3 weeks before 8 Dec.

funding.why_it_fits: Upskill developers (e.g. optimisation, cloud, clinical safety) to build faster.
funding.eligibility_notes: Invest NI clients only; non-mandatory, non-routine training.
funding.next_step: Raise with client executive once an Invest NI client.

funding.fund: Innovate UK Business Growth (formerly Innovate UK EDGE) NI
funding.why_it_fits: Funding and investment-readiness help, Scaleup Programme and Catapult access for health-tech SMEs.
funding.eligibility_notes: Available to all businesses in Northern Ireland; aimed at high-potential innovative SMEs.
funding.next_step: Request an innovation adviser.

funding.amount: Funds a project manager + learning package (amount not stated)

funding.next_step: Book initial assessment with an Innovation Boost consultant.

funding.why_it_fits: Low-cost way to test a technical challenge (e.g. route optimisation) with experts; can lead to Innovation Boost.
funding.eligibility_notes: Eligibility criteria not listed on page – check application pages.

funding.eligibility_notes: Businesses developing new cross-border trade; full criteria on eligibility page.
funding.next_step: Use once product is sale-ready for ROI providers.

funding.why_it_fits: Guidance on growth finance options.

funding.eligibility_notes: UK residents 18+; businesses trading up to 36 months; delivered in NI by Enterprise NI.
funding.next_step: Call Enterprise NI if bridging finance is needed.

funding.fund: R&D tax relief (merged RDEC scheme / ERIS)
funding.amount: RDEC 20% credit; ERIS extra 86% deduction + up to 14.5% payable credit

funding.next_step: Track R&D staff time now; check whether pre-notification to HMRC is needed.

topFive.name: BridgeAI Deployment Catalyst: AI for Operational Systems (Innovate UK)
topFive.why_top_pick: Best UK fit: funds deploying AI that plans and coordinates operations – exactly domiciliary run scheduling to cut mileage/fuel. Opened today.
topFive.practical_steps: 1) Confirm your AI is at TRL 5–6. 2) Sign a UK medium/large deployer (e.g. a large home-care provider). 3) Read IFS brief comp. 2599. 4) Send draft to Invest NI Bid Review (bidreviewservice@investni.com) by mid-Nov. 5) Submit by 11:00, 8 Dec.

topFive.name: Founder Labs (Invest NI / Ormeau Labs)
topFive.why_top_pick: £25k plus a six-month fully funded accelerator, mentoring and investor access – directly speeds up the build.
topFive.practical_steps: 1) Check the £1m / 60% sales-outside-NI / investment tests – frame GB and ROI private care providers as the main market. 2) Apply via Ormeau Labs Founder Labs page. 3) Plan for full-time commitment.

topFive.name: Invest NI Grant for R&D / Project Definition
topFive.why_top_pick: Main NI route to fund software R&D for the HSC-facing platform; rolling, no deadline pressure.
topFive.practical_steps: 1) Call Invest NI 0800 181 4422 to check client eligibility (tradeable services, ≥25% external sales or £250k, 10 staff in 5 yrs). 2) Get a client executive. 3) Scope feasibility/prototype project; ask about TDI (up to £25k) too.

topFive.name: Knowledge Transfer Partnership – Round 4 (Innovate UK)
topFive.why_top_pick: Graduate + QUB/Ulster academic to build routing optimisation and per-run cost analytics; opened this week.
topFive.practical_steps: 1) Contact QUB or Ulster University KTP office now. 2) Agree project scope and business contribution. 3) University submits application by 27 Jan 2027.

topFive.name: Techstart Ventures equity + Co-Fund NI
topFive.why_top_pick: Equity to build faster: Techstart up to £1m initial; Co-Fund matches angels with £150k–£500k typical.
topFive.amount: Up to £1m (Techstart); up to 50% of round (Co-Fund)
topFive.practical_steps: 1) Build deck with HSC discharge/bed-day and fuel-saving evidence. 2) Approach Techstart (techstart.vc/ni). 3) Find an angel lead (HBAN) to unlock Co-Fund NI.
